pages.title: Getting started

fields.objectives: Create a project from the starter; Run the development server; Find your way around the folders

pages.markdown:
Welcome to the course. Over the next nine chapters you will build a small but real dashboard: a page that signs people in, reads invoices from a database and lets them change one.

## Create the project

Open a terminal in the folder you keep your projects in and run:

```bash title="Terminal"
npx create-your-brand-app@latest dashboard --example starter
cd dashboard
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. You should see the starter page with a heading and an empty sidebar.

## What is in the folder

```txt title="dashboard/"
app/          routes, layouts and pages
app/lib/      data helpers and type definitions
public/       pictures served as they are
```

:::hint{style="info"}
Every chapter ends in a working app. If something goes wrong, the solution for that chapter is in the `solutions/` folder of the starter.
:::

pages.title: CSS styling

fields.objectives: Add global styles; Style an element with utility classes

pages.title: Fonts and images

fields.objectives: Load a self-hosted font; Add an image that never shifts the page

pages.markdown:
Fonts and pictures are the two things that most often make a page jump while it loads. The framework handles both for you.

## Fonts

```ts title="app/ui/fonts.ts"
import { localFont } from 'your-brand/font';

export const body = localFont({ src: './inter.woff2', display: 'swap' });
```

The font file ships with your app, so the reader never requests it from anyone else.

## Images

Use the `Image` component with a `width` and `height`. The page reserves the space before the picture arrives, so nothing below it moves.

```tsx title="app/page.tsx"
<Image src="/hero-desktop.png" width={1000} height={760} alt="Screenshots of the dashboard" />
```

modules.name: Routing and data
modules.description: Pages, layouts, links and your first database query.

pages.title: Creating layouts and pages

fields.objectives: Make a route from a folder; Share a layout between pages

pages.markdown:
A folder inside `app/` is a route, and a `page.tsx` inside it is what the route shows. ```txt title="app/" app/dashboard/page.tsx /dashboard app/dashboard/invoices/page.tsx /dashboard/invoices ``` ## A shared layout A `layout.tsx` wraps every page under it. The sidebar goes here, so it stays put while the page beside it changes. ```tsx title="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return (
{children}
); } ```

pages.title: Navigating between pages

fields.objectives: Link between pages without a reload; Highlight the current page

pages.markdown:
Plain `<a>` tags reload the whole page. The `Link` component swaps only what changed.

```tsx title="app/ui/nav-links.tsx"
import Link from 'your-brand/link';

<Link href="/dashboard/invoices">Invoices</Link>
```

## Practice: show the active link

Use the current path to give the active link a different colour.

:::expandable{title="Reveal the solution" style="solution"}
```tsx title="app/ui/nav-links.tsx"
const pathname = usePathname();
<Link className={pathname === link.href ? 'text-blue-600' : ''} href={link.href}>{link.name}</Link>
```
:::

fields.objectives: Query the database from a page; Run independent requests in parallel

pages.title: Streaming

fields.objectives: Stream a slow part of the page; Draw a skeleton that does not shift the layout

pages.markdown:
A slow query should not hold up the whole page. Wrap the slow part in `Suspense` and show a skeleton the same size until it arrives.

```tsx title="app/dashboard/page.tsx"
<Suspense fallback={<RevenueChartSkeleton />}>
  <RevenueChart />
</Suspense>
```

The skeleton must take the same space as the chart, so nothing moves when the real chart replaces it.

pages.title: Deploying your app

fields.objectives: Deploy from Git; Configure environment variables

pages.markdown:
You have a dashboard that reads, streams and writes. Time to put it online.

1. Push the project to a Git repository.
2. Import it in Your Brand Cloud and add the database's connection string as an environment variable.
3. Every push to `main` now deploys, and every branch gets a preview address.

Congratulations: you have finished the course. Take the final check below to earn your certificate.

questions.prompt: Where can a page read the database directly?
questions.explanation: Pages are server components by default, so the query runs on the server.

questions.prompt: Two requests do not depend on each other. How should you start them?
questions.explanation: Started together, the page waits for the slowest one instead of the sum of both.

questions.prompt: What should a Suspense fallback look like?
choices: A skeleton the same size as the content
questions.explanation: A skeleton of the same size means nothing moves when the content arrives.

questions.prompt: Where does a server action run?
questions.explanation: That is why it can talk to the database directly.

questions.prompt: Which of these does a deploy from Git give you?
choices: Production on every push to main
questions.explanation: Branches get previews; main goes to production. The database is yours to configure.
